answer: Entry runs through a mesa gate priced by congestion: every newcomer in the same window buys a saffron ticket whose price grows with the square of that window's entrant count, and the proceeds feed an umber audit reserve that randomly re-checks entrants after entry. A lone honest agent pays a small fee, but an operator flooding the gate with n clones pays n tickets at a price squared in n, so total cost grows roughly cubically and cannot be split across clones, since each ticket is tied to one identity and burns on use.
